content.text:
Since the object color signature can include inner colors, I'll keep things simple by using hollow boxes for most examples, plus maybe one with a uniquely colored interior to demonstrate that "anything inside" still counts toward the match. Now I'm sketching out the three color pairs to build these test cases.

For pair one, I'll place a 3-colored box duplicated twice alongside single 4 and 6 boxes, keeping the 4 and 6 as they're unique colors. For pair two, I want a box with a nested inner dot of a different color to test that the outer box is still recognized despite the different interior. For pair three, I'll set up three identical boxes of one color that get erased, leaving a single differently-colored box behind. I'm now working out exact grid coordinates to place each of these boxes cleanly across roughly 12-14 cell grids.
